docs.title: Welcome to Brindlewood Instruments
docs.text:
# Welcome to Brindlewood Instruments

## About this handbook

Brindlewood Instruments designs and builds industrial sensors: vibration monitors for wind turbines, flow meters for water utilities and the Kestrel range of handheld gas detectors. We have about 640 employees across three sites: the headquarters and main factory in Harrowgate, the firmware and cloud team in Velmont, and a small sales and service office in Port Aster.

This handbook collects the policies that apply to everyone who works here. It is written in plain language on purpose. Where a policy needs a form, the form code is given so you can find it in the Brindlewood portal. Where a rule differs between sites, the difference is stated in the section that applies.

The handbook is owned by the People Team. Each policy also has a named policy owner, listed at the end of that policy, who answers detailed questions and approves exceptions. If a local law gives you a better deal than this handbook, the law wins.

## How policies change

Policies are reviewed at least once a year. Changes are announced on the company noticeboard channel two weeks before they take effect, except for changes that are required by law or that fix a safety problem, which take effect immediately.

The version of a policy that applies is the one in force on the day the event happened. For example, an expense is judged under the travel policy that applied on the day you spent the money, not the day you submitted the claim.

## Who to ask

Start with your manager. For anything about pay, leave or benefits, contact the People Team through the HR desk in the portal. For laptops, accounts and security, raise a ticket with the IT Service Desk. For anything that worries you about safety, stop the work and tell the site safety lead straight away; you never need permission to stop unsafe work.

## Core values

We say four things about how we work. We measure before we argue, because our business is measurement. We fix the cause, not the symptom. We tell customers the truth about what our instruments can and cannot do. And we leave every site, file and process a little better than we found it.

These values are not decoration. Managers are asked to use them when they give feedback, and they appear in the performance review form.

docs.title: Working Hours and Attendance
docs.text:
# Working Hours and Attendance

## Standard hours

The standard working week is 37.5 hours for full-time staff, usually worked Monday to Friday. Factory shifts in Harrowgate follow the shift rota instead, which is published four weeks ahead by the production planning team.

## Core hours

Office-based staff may choose their own start and finish times, provided they are available during core hours. Core hours are 10:00 to 15:00 local time, Monday to Thursday, and 10:00 to 13:00 on Friday. Meetings that need the whole team should be booked inside core hours so that people with caring responsibilities can attend.

## Overtime

Overtime only applies to roles that are paid by the hour. Overtime must be approved in advance by your manager using form HR-220, except during a declared production emergency. Approved overtime is paid at 1.5 times the normal hourly rate on weekdays and twice the normal hourly rate on Sundays and public holidays. Salaried staff do not receive overtime pay; instead, if you regularly work beyond your contracted hours, talk to your manager about time off in lieu.

## Time off in lieu

Time off in lieu, which we call TOIL, is available to salaried staff who work at a weekend or on a public holiday at the company's request. You earn one hour of TOIL for every hour worked. TOIL must be taken within three months of being earned and cannot be paid out as money, except when you leave the company.

## Lateness and absence

If you are going to be late or absent and you have not booked leave, tell your manager before your start time, or as soon as you safely can. Factory staff must also tell the shift supervisor, because a missing person on a line changes the staffing plan. Repeated unexplained absence is handled under the conduct policy.

## Breaks

Everyone working more than six hours in a day is entitled to an unpaid break of at least 30 minutes. Factory staff also get two paid ten-minute breaks per shift. People who work at screens for long periods are encouraged to take a short pause away from the screen every hour.

Policy owner: Head of People Operations.

docs.title: Leave and Time Off
docs.text:
# Leave and Time Off

## Annual leave entitlement

Full-time employees receive 25 days of paid annual leave per leave year, plus public holidays. The leave year runs from 1 April to 31 March. Part-time employees receive the same entitlement in proportion to the hours in their contract. After five complete years of service your entitlement rises to 27 days, and after ten complete years it rises to 30 days.

## Booking leave

Book leave in the portal as early as you can. Requests for up to three consecutive days need one week of notice; longer requests need notice of at least twice the length of the leave. Managers should answer a leave request within five working days. In the factory, no more than two people from the same line may be on leave on the same day, so popular weeks are allocated in the order requests arrive.

## Carrying leave over

You may carry over up to five days of unused annual leave into the next leave year. Carried-over days must be used by 30 June of the new leave year, after which they expire without payment. If you could not take leave because you were on long-term sick leave or parental leave, the five-day limit does not apply and your manager will agree a plan with the People Team.

## Buying and selling leave

Once a year, during the benefits window in February, you may buy up to five extra days of leave through salary sacrifice. Selling leave back to the company is not allowed, because rest is the point of leave.

## Public holidays

Each site observes the public holidays of its country. In addition, the whole company closes on the working days between 25 December and 1 January; these closure days are given on top of your annual leave and are not deducted from it. Staff who must work during the closure, such as the on-call engineers, receive a day of TOIL for each closure day worked.

## Sick leave

If you are ill, tell your manager before your start time on the first day. For absences of up to seven calendar days you can self-certify in the portal when you return. For absences longer than seven calendar days you need a doctor's note, uploaded with form HR-114. Company sick pay is full pay for the first 20 working days of sickness in any rolling twelve-month period, then half pay for the next 20 working days, after which statutory sick pay applies.

## Return to work

After any absence of more than two weeks, your manager will hold a short return-to-work conversation. The purpose is to check whether you need any adjustments, such as a phased return or different duties, and not to question whether you were ill.

## Parental leave

Birth parents receive 26 weeks of parental leave at full pay, followed by up to 26 more weeks of unpaid leave. Partners and adoptive parents receive 12 weeks at full pay. Parental leave at full pay requires six months of continuous service at the expected date of birth or placement. You can take partner leave in up to three blocks within the first year.

## Bereavement and compassionate leave

If a close family member dies, you may take up to ten days of paid bereavement leave. For the loss of a pregnancy, either parent may take up to ten days of paid leave. Managers may grant further compassionate leave for other serious family situations; it does not need to be justified in detail.

## Jury service and volunteering

Jury service is paid as normal working time. You also get two paid volunteering days per year to support a registered charity or a school.

Policy owner: Head of People Operations.

docs.title: Remote and Hybrid Work
docs.text:
# Remote and Hybrid Work

## Who can work remotely

Roles are classified as site-based, hybrid or remote. Factory, laboratory and facilities roles are site-based. Most office roles are hybrid, which means at least two days per week at your home site, chosen with your team. Remote roles are approved by a director and are listed in your contract.

## Anchor days

Each team agrees one anchor day per week when everyone in the team is on site. Anchor days are for planning, design reviews and the kind of conversation that is harder over video. Please do not book leave on your team's anchor day unless it cannot be avoided.

## Your home workspace

Before you work from home regularly, complete the home workspace self-assessment in the portal. Hybrid and remote staff may claim a one-off home office allowance of 400 for a desk, chair or monitor, using form EXP-12. The allowance can be claimed once every four years. Laptops, docking stations and headsets are supplied by IT and stay company property.

## Working from another country

You may work from a country other than your contracted country for up to 20 working days in any rolling twelve-month period, provided the country is on the approved list in the portal. You must submit form HR-305 at least three weeks before you travel, so that the People Team and Legal can check tax and immigration rules. Working from a country that is not on the approved list is not allowed, even for a single day, because it can create a tax presence for the company.

## Security when working away from the office

Never work on Restricted data in a public place such as a train, café or airport lounge. Use the company VPN on any network that is not the office network. Lock your screen whenever you step away, even at home.

## Costs of working from home

Brindlewood does not pay for home internet or electricity for hybrid staff. Remote staff receive a monthly connectivity allowance of 30, paid with salary.

## Changing your working pattern

Anyone with at least 26 weeks of service may request a change to their hours, days or place of work. Submit the request with form HR-310. Your manager must meet you to discuss it within 28 days and give a written decision with reasons. If the request is refused, you may appeal once within 14 days.

Policy owner: Director of Workplace.

docs.title: Travel and Expenses
docs.text:
# Travel and Expenses

## Principles

Spend company money as if it were your own, and only when travel is the best way to get the work done. A video call is often enough. When you do travel, choose the option that gives the best value overall, which is not always the cheapest ticket.

## Approval before travel

All business travel must be approved by your manager before you book. International travel also needs approval from your director. Book flights, trains and hotels through the company travel desk so that we know where people are if there is an emergency; bookings made elsewhere are only refunded if they were at least ten percent cheaper than the travel desk price for the same journey.

## Flights and trains

Economy class is the standard for all flights. Premium economy is allowed for a single flight segment longer than six hours. Business class is only allowed for flights longer than ten hours when you are expected to work on the day you land, and it needs director approval in writing. For journeys under four hours, take the train where a direct train exists.

## Hotels

Hotels must be booked through the travel desk within the nightly cap for the city. The cap is 160 per night in most cities and 220 per night in the high-cost cities listed in the portal. If the only hotels near a customer site are above the cap, the travel desk can approve an exception before you book.

## Daily allowance

Instead of claiming every meal, travellers receive a daily allowance, called the per-diem, which covers meals, drinks and small incidental costs. The per-diem depends on the destination zone. Zone A covers domestic travel and pays 45 per day. Zone B covers most of Europe and pays 60 per day. Zone C covers North America, Japan, Singapore and Australia and pays 80 per day. If a customer or conference provides a meal, reduce the per-diem by 15 for each meal provided. On the day you travel out and the day you travel back, you receive 75 percent of the per-diem.

## Mileage

If you use your own car for business, claim mileage at 0.45 per mile for the first 10,000 business miles in a tax year and 0.25 per mile after that. Commuting between your home and your normal site is not business mileage. Parking and tolls are reimbursed with a receipt.

## Submitting claims

Submit expense claims with form EXP-7 within 60 days of the date you spent the money. Each item over 25 needs an itemised receipt; a photograph of the receipt is fine. Claims submitted later than 60 days are only paid if your director approves the delay. Approved claims are paid with the next monthly salary run if they are approved before the 15th of the month.

## Corporate cards

Employees who travel more than six times a year may apply for a corporate card. The corporate card must only be used for business costs. If a personal cost is charged to the card by mistake, report it within seven days and the amount will be deducted from your next salary.

## What we do not reimburse

We do not pay for upgrades you choose yourself, minibar items, traffic or parking fines, personal entertainment, or lost luggage that is covered by the airline. Alcohol is only reimbursed as part of an approved client meal.

Policy owner: Finance Controller.

docs.title: IT Equipment and Security
docs.text:
# IT Equipment and Security

## Your equipment

Every employee receives a laptop configured by IT. Engineers may choose between two standard models; everyone else receives the standard business laptop. Laptops are replaced every four years, or sooner if they fail. Do not install software that is not in the company software catalogue; if you need something that is missing, request it through the IT Service Desk and it will be reviewed within five working days.

## Passwords and sign-in

Use the company password manager for every work account. Passwords must be at least 14 characters long and must not be reused between accounts. Multi-factor authentication is required for email, the portal, the source code host and the cloud consoles. A hardware security key is required for anyone with administrator access to production systems; IT issues two keys, one for daily use and one kept somewhere safe as a backup.

## Lost or stolen devices

If your laptop, phone or security key is lost or stolen, report it to the IT Service Desk within one hour of noticing, by phone if you cannot reach the portal. IT will lock the device remotely and revoke its access. Reporting quickly matters more than anything else; nobody is disciplined for losing a device, but delayed reporting is treated as a security incident in its own right.

## Phishing and suspicious messages

If an email, message or call asks you to act urgently, to share a code, or to pay an invoice to new bank details, treat it as suspicious. Use the Report Phish button in your email client. Never approve a multi-factor prompt that you did not start yourself. Finance will never change a supplier's bank details because of an email alone; changes are always confirmed by a call to a number already on file.

## Security incidents

A security incident is any event that may have exposed company or customer data, or allowed someone unauthorised access. Report suspected incidents to the security team through the incident form IT-3, or by calling the security line if the incident is ongoing. Do not try to investigate on your own and do not delete anything, because evidence may be needed.

## Personal devices

You may read email and chat on a personal phone if you enrol it in the mobile device management app, which can wipe company data but not your personal data. Personal laptops must never be used to access source code, customer data or production systems.

## Removable media

USB storage devices are blocked on company laptops. If a customer gives you data on a USB stick, take it to IT, who will scan it on an isolated machine and transfer the files for you.

## Software updates

Laptops install security updates automatically. When an update needs a restart, you can postpone it for up to 72 hours; after that the laptop restarts on its own outside core hours.

Policy owner: Chief Information Security Officer.

docs.title: Data Classification and Handling
docs.text:
# Data Classification and Handling

## Why we classify data

Not all information needs the same protection. Classifying data tells everyone how carefully to handle it, so that we protect what matters without slowing down everything else.

## The four levels

Public data, level L0, is information we have chosen to publish, such as datasheets and press releases. Internal data, level L1, is everyday business information that would cause little harm if it leaked, such as the canteen menu or team meeting notes. Confidential data, level L2, would harm the company or a customer if it leaked; examples are pricing, contracts, unreleased product plans and source code. Restricted data, level L3, would cause serious harm and is subject to legal duties; examples are personal data about employees or customers, health information, payroll records and customer calibration certificates that identify a site.

## Labelling

Documents at L2 and L3 must carry their classification in the header or file name. Email containing L3 data must be marked Restricted in the subject line. Anything unlabelled is treated as Internal until its owner classifies it.

## Storing data

L0 and L1 data may be stored in any company system. L2 data must stay in approved company systems and must not be copied to personal accounts. L3 data may only be stored in systems that are on the Restricted register, which IT publishes in the portal, and access must be limited to people who need it for their job.

## Sharing outside the company

L2 data may be shared with a customer or supplier only under a signed non-disclosure agreement. L3 data may only be shared outside the company after the Data Protection Officer has approved a data sharing agreement, and it must be sent through the secure file transfer service, never as an email attachment.

## Retention and deletion

Keep data only for as long as it is needed. Customer calibration certificates are kept for seven years after the instrument is retired, because customers rely on them in audits. Recruitment records for unsuccessful candidates are deleted twelve months after the role is filled. Payroll records are kept for six years after the end of the tax year they relate to.

## Using AI tools with company data

Only the AI assistants listed in the software catalogue may be used with company data. L0 and L1 data may be used with any catalogue assistant. L2 data may only be used with the assistants marked as approved for Confidential data, which do not keep or train on what you send. L3 data must never be pasted into any AI assistant.

## Requests from individuals

If someone asks to see, correct or delete the personal data we hold about them, forward the request to the Data Protection Officer on the same day. We have one month to respond, so the clock starts as soon as anyone at Brindlewood receives the request.

Policy owner: Data Protection Officer.

docs.title: Code of Conduct
docs.text:
# Code of Conduct

## Respect at work

Treat everyone with respect, whatever their role, background or opinions. Harassment, bullying and discrimination are not tolerated, whether in person, in chat, or at work social events. If you see behaviour that crosses the line, you are encouraged to say something or to report it; you will not be penalised for a report made in good faith.

## Gifts and hospitality

You may accept small gifts from customers or suppliers, such as a branded notebook or a box of sweets for the team, if they are worth less than 50. Gifts worth 50 or more must be declared in the gifts register within five working days and are normally declined politely or shared with the team by raffle. Hospitality such as a meal or a match ticket must be declared if it is worth more than 100. Never accept cash or vouchers, whatever the amount, and never accept anything from a supplier during a tender you are involved in.

## Giving gifts

Gifts to customers must be modest and must be recorded by the account manager. Gifts or hospitality for public officials, including employees of publicly owned water utilities, need prior approval from the Legal team, because anti-bribery law treats them strictly.

## Conflicts of interest

A conflict of interest arises when your personal interests could influence, or look as if they influence, your work decisions. Examples include hiring a relative, owning shares in a supplier, or having a second job with a competitor. Declare any actual or potential conflict to your manager and in the conflicts register as soon as you become aware of it. Having a conflict is not wrongdoing; hiding one is.

## Second jobs

You may have a second job or run a business outside work, provided it does not compete with Brindlewood, does not use company time or equipment, and does not affect your ability to do your job. Tell your manager before you start.

## Social media

You may say that you work at Brindlewood. Do not share Confidential or Restricted information, do not speak on behalf of the company unless you are authorised to, and make clear that opinions are your own. Customer names may only be mentioned if they appear on our published reference list.

## Alcohol and drugs

Do not work under the influence of alcohol or drugs. Anyone working in the factory, the laboratory or driving for work must not drink alcohol before or during their shift. If prescribed medicine may affect your ability to work safely, tell your manager or the site safety lead.

## Breaches of the code

Breaches are handled under the disciplinary procedure, which starts with an investigation and gives you the right to be accompanied at any formal meeting.

Policy owner: General Counsel.

docs.title: Performance and Career Development
docs.text:
# Performance and Career Development

## The review cycle

Brindlewood runs two review conversations each year. The mid-year check-in happens in October and is a conversation about progress and support, with no rating. The annual review happens in April and includes a rating, which feeds into pay decisions. New starters who joined less than three months before a review are not rated in that cycle.

## Objectives

At the start of each review year, agree three to five objectives with your manager. At least one objective should be about learning or helping others learn. Objectives can change during the year when priorities change; record the change in the portal so that you are reviewed against what you were actually asked to do.

## Ratings

The annual rating uses four levels: Exceptional, Strong, Developing and Below expectations. Ratings are calibrated in a meeting of managers in each department, so that a Strong in one team means the same as a Strong in another. There is no quota for any rating.

## Feedback from colleagues

Before the annual review, you choose three to five colleagues to give written feedback. Your manager may add one more. Feedback is shared with you in summary, without names, unless the colleague chooses to sign it.

## Promotion

Promotions are decided twice a year, in April and October. Your manager nominates you with a short written case that shows you are already working at the next level for at least six months. A promotion panel from outside your immediate team reviews each case. If a nomination is not approved, the panel gives written feedback about what evidence was missing, and you may be nominated again in the next round.

## Career levels

Engineering and product roles follow the technical ladder from level T1 to T7, and people managers follow the management ladder from M3 to M6. Moving between ladders is a sideways move, not a promotion, and keeps your pay.

## Learning budget

Each employee has an annual learning budget of 1,200 for courses, conferences, books and certifications that are relevant to their role. Managers approve spending from the budget; anything over 600 in a single item also needs approval from the department head. Unused budget does not roll over to the next year. If the company pays more than 2,000 for a single certification and you leave within twelve months, you may be asked to repay part of the cost.

## Underperformance

If performance falls below expectations, your manager will first discuss it informally and agree support. If that does not help, a formal performance improvement plan of at least eight weeks is agreed in writing, with clear goals and regular check-ins.

Policy owner: Head of Talent.

docs.title: Pay and Benefits
docs.text:
# Pay and Benefits

## Pay dates

Salaries are paid monthly on the 25th of each month. If the 25th falls on a weekend or public holiday, pay arrives on the last working day before it. Payslips are published in the portal three days before pay day. Hourly paid factory staff are paid on the same day for hours worked up to the 10th of that month.

## Annual pay review

Pay is reviewed once a year, with any change taking effect on 1 July. The review considers your annual rating, the market rate for your role and the company's results. Employees on a performance improvement plan at the time of the review are reviewed again when the plan ends.

## Pension

All employees are enrolled in the company pension plan. Brindlewood matches your contribution up to 6 percent of salary, and adds a further 1 percent for employees with more than five years of service. You may opt out, but you will lose the company contribution while you are opted out. You can change your contribution once a month in the portal.

## Health insurance

Private health insurance is provided for all employees after their probation period. You may add a partner or children to the policy at your own cost, which is deducted from salary before tax. Dental cover is included; optical cover is a voluntary extra.

## Employee assistance programme

The employee assistance programme offers free, confidential counselling, legal and financial advice, 24 hours a day. You can use it without telling anyone at Brindlewood, and the company receives only anonymous usage statistics.

## Bonus

The annual bonus pool depends on company profit for the financial year. Individual bonus depends on your annual rating, and is paid with the July salary to employees who are still employed on 30 June and are not serving notice.

## Share scheme

Every year in September, employees may join the share save plan, saving between 10 and 250 per month for three years. At the end of the three years, you can buy shares at the price fixed when you joined, or take your savings back.

## Cycle to work and electric cars

You may lease a bicycle or an electric car through salary sacrifice. Cycle leases are limited to a value of 2,500. Electric car leases are available after probation and require a minimum lease of two years.

## Probation

New employees have a probation period of six months. During probation, the notice period on both sides is two weeks. Probation can be extended once by up to three months if more time is needed to assess the role.

Policy owner: Head of Reward.

docs.title: On-call and Incident Response
docs.text:
# On-call and Incident Response

## Who is on call

Engineers in the cloud platform, firmware release and device fleet teams take part in on-call rotations once they have completed three months of service and shadowed two full shifts. Each rotation has a primary and a secondary engineer. A rotation lasts one week, starting Tuesday at 10:00, so that handovers happen in core hours and not on a Monday after a weekend.

## On-call pay

Engineers on call receive a standby payment of 40 per weekday night and 90 per weekend day or public holiday. If you are paged and work on an incident outside your normal hours, you also earn TOIL equal to the time spent, rounded up to the next half hour. Nobody should be on call for more than one week in four.

## Response times

When you are paged, acknowledge the page within 15 minutes. If the primary does not acknowledge within 15 minutes, the page goes to the secondary, and after a further 15 minutes it goes to the engineering manager on duty. You must be able to reach a laptop and a stable connection within 30 minutes while on call.

## Severity levels

SEV1 means customers cannot receive alarm data from their instruments, or a safety alert may be delayed. SEV2 means a major feature is broken for many customers, but alarm delivery works. SEV3 means a minor problem with a workaround. A SEV1 must be declared in the incident channel immediately, and an incident commander must be named within ten minutes. Gas detector alarm delivery is always treated as SEV1, whatever the number of customers affected.

## Running an incident

The incident commander coordinates and does not debug. A separate communications lead updates the status page every 30 minutes during a SEV1. Write down what you try and when in the incident channel, because the timeline is needed afterwards.

## After the incident

Every SEV1 and SEV2 incident has a blameless review within five working days. The review produces a written timeline, the contributing causes, and actions with owners and dates. The aim is to fix systems and processes, not to find a person to blame.

## Rest after incidents

If you are paged between midnight and 06:00 and work for more than an hour, start late the next day by at least as long as you worked. You do not need to ask permission; just tell your team.

Policy owner: VP Engineering.

docs.title: Facilities and Sites
docs.text:
# Facilities and Sites

## Badges and access

Your photo badge opens the doors you need for your role. Wear it visibly at all times on site. If you lose your badge, report it to reception the same day so that it can be cancelled; a replacement costs nothing the first time and 15 for each further replacement. Never hold a secure door open for someone you do not recognise.

## Visitors

Register visitors in the portal at least one working day before they arrive. Visitors sign in at reception, receive a visitor badge and must be accompanied at all times in the factory and the laboratory. Visitors who will enter the factory floor must watch the five-minute safety video at reception before they go in.

## Parking

Harrowgate has staff parking on a first come, first served basis, with reserved spaces for blue badge holders, expectant parents and car sharers. Velmont has no staff parking; staff there receive a discounted public transport pass instead. Electric vehicle chargers are free to use, but please move your car once it is charged so others can use the charger.

## Pets

Pets are not allowed in the factory, the laboratory or the canteen at any site. The Velmont office allows well-behaved dogs on Fridays only, in the open-plan area on the second floor, provided the owner has registered the dog with reception and colleagues on that floor have not raised an allergy concern. Assistance dogs are welcome at all sites and in all areas except the clean room.

## Meeting rooms and desks

Desks at Velmont and Port Aster are shared and booked in the portal. Clear your desk at the end of the day; anything left overnight is moved to lost property. Meeting rooms can be booked for up to two hours at a time, and recurring bookings expire after three months unless renewed.

## Canteen and kitchens

The Harrowgate canteen serves subsidised breakfast and lunch on working days. Free fruit and hot drinks are available at all sites. Label any food you leave in a shared fridge with your name and the date; unlabelled food is thrown away every Friday afternoon.

## Reporting a problem

Report broken equipment, heating problems or cleaning issues through the facilities request form FAC-2. Urgent problems that affect safety, such as a water leak near electrical equipment, should be reported to reception by phone.

## Fire safety

Fire alarms are tested every Wednesday at 11:00 at Harrowgate and every Thursday at 09:30 at Velmont; a test lasts no more than one minute. At any other time, an alarm means leave the building immediately by the nearest exit and go to the assembly point. Fire wardens check each floor and report to the site safety lead. Do not go back inside until the site safety lead says it is safe.

Policy owner: Director of Workplace.

docs.title: Purchasing and Suppliers
docs.text:
# Purchasing and Suppliers

## Spending limits

Every purchase needs a purchase order raised in the portal before the supplier is asked to deliver. Purchases up to 1,000 can be approved by your manager. Purchases above 1,000 and up to 10,000 need approval from the budget holder for the department. Purchases above 10,000 and up to 50,000 need approval from the Finance Controller as well. Anything above 50,000 needs three written quotes and approval from the Chief Financial Officer.

## Splitting orders

Splitting a purchase into smaller orders to stay under an approval limit is not allowed. Orders to the same supplier for the same project within 30 days are added together when deciding which approval level applies.

## Choosing suppliers

Use a supplier from the approved supplier list where one exists for what you need. New suppliers must pass a due diligence check covering finances, data protection and modern slavery before their first order. For electronic components, suppliers must also be able to show the origin of the parts, because counterfeit components are a known risk in our industry.

## Software and cloud services

Any new software or cloud service, including free tools and trials, must be reviewed by IT and Security before use, even if no money changes hands. This is because many free tools collect data. Request a review through the IT Service Desk with the tool name, what you will use it for and the classification of the data involved.

## Paying suppliers

Our standard payment terms are 45 days from the date of a valid invoice. Small suppliers with fewer than 50 employees are paid within 21 days. Invoices must quote the purchase order number; invoices without one are returned to the supplier unpaid.

## Contracts

Only people listed in the signing authority register may sign contracts on behalf of Brindlewood. Clicking accept on online terms counts as signing a contract, so check the register before you accept terms for a paid service.

Policy owner: Finance Controller.

docs.title: Joining and Leaving
docs.text:
# Joining and Leaving

## Before your first day

New starters receive their contract, the handbook and a link to the onboarding portal before their first day. Bring proof of your right to work on day one; the People Team must check the original document before you start work.

## Your first weeks

Every new starter has an onboarding buddy from a different team for their first three months. In the first week you complete the mandatory training: health and safety, information security, data protection and the code of conduct. Factory and laboratory staff also complete site-specific safety induction before they touch any equipment.

## Probation reviews

Your manager meets you at the end of your first, third and fifth months to review how probation is going. The final probation decision is made before the end of the sixth month and is confirmed in writing.

## Resigning

To resign, tell your manager and confirm it in writing through the portal. Notice periods are set in your contract: usually one month for roles up to level T3, and three months for senior roles. During probation the notice period is two weeks.

## Your last weeks

Your manager will agree a handover plan with you. Any annual leave you have not taken is paid with your final salary; leave you have taken beyond your earned entitlement is deducted from it. You may be asked to take outstanding leave during your notice period.

## Returning equipment

Return your laptop, badge, security keys and any other company property on or before your last day. Remote staff receive a prepaid courier box. Equipment that is not returned within 14 days of your last day may be deducted from your final pay at its current value.

## Account closure

Your accounts are disabled at 17:00 on your last working day. Your email is forwarded to your manager for 30 days and then deleted. Before you leave, move any files your team will need into shared team folders; personal folders are deleted 30 days after you leave.

## Exit conversation

Everyone who leaves is offered an exit conversation with the People Team, separate from their manager. What you say is used, without your name, to improve how we work.

## Rehiring

People who left on good terms are welcome to apply again. If you rejoin within twelve months, your previous service counts towards leave entitlement and pension matching.

Policy owner: Head of People Operations.

docs.title: Health and Safety
docs.text:
# Health and Safety

## Everyone's responsibility

Everyone is responsible for working safely and for not putting others at risk. You have the right and the duty to stop any work you believe is unsafe. Stopping work for safety reasons will never count against you, even if it turns out there was no danger.

## Reporting accidents and near misses

Report every accident, injury or near miss through the safety reporting form HS-1 before the end of your shift. A near miss is an event that could have caused harm but did not, such as a dropped tool that landed next to someone. Near misses are the most useful reports we get, because they let us fix a problem before anyone is hurt.

## First aid

Each site has trained first aiders, listed on the noticeboard by every exit. First aid kits are in every kitchen and on every factory line. Eye wash stations are in the laboratory and next to the battery assembly area.

## Personal protective equipment

Safety glasses and safety shoes are required on the factory floor at all times. Hearing protection is required in the test hall when the shaker table is running, which is shown by an amber light above the door. The company provides all required protective equipment free of charge; prescription safety glasses are provided up to a cost of 150 per year.

## The calibration laboratory

The calibration laboratory uses certified reference gases, some of which are toxic or flammable. Only staff who hold a current gas handling certificate may connect or change gas cylinders. Two people must be present whenever a toxic reference gas is in use, and the fixed gas monitors in the laboratory must be checked at the start of every shift. If a fixed monitor alarms, leave the laboratory, close the door and call the site safety lead; do not go back in to switch anything off.

## Lone working

Lone working in the factory or the laboratory outside normal hours is only allowed for tasks on the approved lone-working list, and only after you have checked in with security. Security will call you every hour; if you do not answer, they will come to find you.

## Display screen equipment

If you work at a screen for more than an hour a day, complete the workstation assessment in the portal. Employees who need glasses specifically for screen work can claim the cost of an eye test and up to 80 towards glasses.

## Driving for work

If you drive for work, your licence is checked every year. Do not take calls while driving, even hands-free, unless the call is an emergency. Plan journeys so that you take a 15-minute break at least every two hours.

## Stress and wellbeing

Workload pressure is a health and safety matter too. If your workload is making you unwell, tell your manager or the People Team; they can complete a stress risk assessment with you and agree changes.

Policy owner: Head of Health, Safety and Environment.

docs.title: Product Quality and Customer Returns
docs.text:
# Product Quality and Customer Returns

## Quality comes first

Our instruments protect people and infrastructure. A gas detector that reads low can hurt someone, and a vibration monitor that misses a failing bearing can cost a customer a turbine. Nobody at Brindlewood is ever asked to ship a product they believe is unsafe or out of specification.

## Raising a quality concern

Anyone who suspects a defect in a shipped or finished product must raise a quality concern with form QA-9 on the same working day. Describe what you saw, the serial numbers involved and how you found it. The quality team acknowledges every concern within one working day and decides whether to place affected stock on hold.

## Stock on hold

Stock placed on hold is marked with a red hold label and moved to the quarantine cage. It may only be released by a quality engineer, who records the reason in the quality system. Moving or shipping held stock without that release is a serious breach of this policy.

## Customer complaints

Customer complaints arrive through the service desk, account managers and the website. Whoever receives a complaint logs it in the complaints system within one working day, even if it seems minor or the customer has already been helped. Complaints that suggest a safety risk are escalated to the Head of Quality immediately by phone.

## Returns and repairs

Customers return instruments for repair or replacement using a return authorisation number, which the service desk issues before anything is shipped. Instruments returned without a return authorisation number are held at goods-in and the customer is contacted; they are not opened until the paperwork is complete. Instruments returned from a site where they may have been exposed to hazardous substances must be decontaminated by the customer and come with a signed decontamination declaration.

## Warranty

Kestrel gas detectors carry a two-year warranty. Vibration monitors and flow meters carry a three-year warranty, extended to five years for customers with an active service contract. The warranty does not cover damage caused by use outside the published operating range, or sensors that have reached the end of their rated life.

## Field safety notices

If a defect could affect safety in the field, the Head of Quality may issue a field safety notice. A field safety notice tells customers what is wrong, what they should do now and how we will fix it. Customers are told within 48 hours of the decision to issue a notice, and regulators are told within the time their rules require.

## Recalls and the recall team

A recall is coordinated by a recall team chaired by the Head of Quality, with members from service, sales, legal and communications. The recall team meets every working day until the last affected instrument has been traced. Account managers contact each affected customer personally; a mass email is never enough on its own.

## Calibration certificates

Every instrument leaves the factory with a calibration certificate that is traceable to national standards. Certificates are signed by an authorised calibration technician and stored in the certificate archive. A certificate may never be edited after it has been issued; if it contains a mistake, a corrected certificate is issued with a new number and the old one is marked as withdrawn.

## Audits

We are audited by our certification body every year and by large customers when they ask. Treat auditors politely, answer the question they asked, and if you do not know the answer, say so and offer to find out. Never create or change a record because an audit is coming.

Policy owner: Head of Quality.

docs.title: Inclusion, Accessibility and Adjustments
docs.text:
# Inclusion, Accessibility and Adjustments

## Our commitment

We want everyone to be able to do their best work here. That means hiring fairly, paying fairly, and removing barriers that make work harder for some people than for others.

## Workplace adjustments

If a disability, a long-term health condition or neurodivergence makes some part of your job harder, you can ask for a workplace adjustment. Examples include a different chair or screen, speech-to-text software, written agendas before meetings, a quieter desk, or changed working hours. You do not need a formal diagnosis to ask. Talk to your manager or the People Team, or use the adjustments form HR-150 if you prefer to write it down.

## How requests are handled

Your manager meets you to understand what would help, and may ask an occupational health adviser for advice with your consent. Simple adjustments, such as equipment under 500, should be in place within two weeks of the request. Adjustments are recorded in an adjustments passport, which you own and which moves with you if you change team, so that you do not have to explain your needs again.

## Recruitment

Every job advert says that candidates can ask for adjustments to the interview process. Interview panels include at least two people, and at least one of them has completed the fair hiring course. Interview questions are prepared in advance and every candidate for the same role is asked the same core questions.

## Pay equality

We publish a pay gap report every year. Each annual pay review includes a check for unexplained pay differences between people doing equal work, and any difference that cannot be explained is corrected in that review.

## Religious observance

You may use flexible hours or annual leave for religious festivals. Quiet rooms for prayer and reflection are available at Harrowgate and Velmont and can be used without booking.

## Menopause and reproductive health

Menopause symptoms, fertility treatment and pregnancy-related illness are treated with the same care as any other health matter. You may take paid time off for fertility treatment appointments, up to five appointments per treatment cycle.

## Employee networks

Employee networks run with company support and a small annual budget. Current networks include the disability and neurodiversity network, the parents and carers network, the women in engineering network and the pride network. Network leads may spend up to two hours a week of work time on network activity.

## Reporting discrimination

If you experience or see discrimination, report it to your manager, the People Team or through the speak-up line. Reports are investigated promptly and confidentially, and nobody may be treated badly for making a report in good faith.

Policy owner: Head of Inclusion.

docs.title: Speaking Up, Grievances and Discipline
docs.text:
# Speaking Up, Grievances and Discipline

## Speaking up about wrongdoing

If you believe something seriously wrong is happening at Brindlewood, such as fraud, a danger to health or safety, a breach of the law, falsified test results or a cover-up of any of these, you should speak up. You can raise it with your manager, with a director, or through the independent speak-up line, which is run by an outside provider and can be used anonymously by phone or online.

## Protection for people who speak up

Nobody may be dismissed, disciplined, refused promotion or treated worse because they raised a concern in good faith, even if the concern turns out to be mistaken. Retaliating against someone who has spoken up is itself a disciplinary offence. If you think you are being treated badly because you spoke up, tell the General Counsel directly.

## What happens next

Concerns raised through the speak-up line are passed to the General Counsel and the chair of the audit committee, never to the person the concern is about. You will receive an acknowledgement within seven days and an update on progress within 30 days, although we cannot always share the outcome if it involves other people's confidential information.

## Raising a grievance

A grievance is a concern or complaint about your own work, working conditions or relationships with colleagues. Try to resolve it informally with your manager first. If that does not work, or the grievance is about your manager, raise a formal grievance in writing with the People Team using form HR-400. A grievance meeting will be held within ten working days, and you may bring a colleague or a trade union representative.

## Grievance appeals

If you are unhappy with the outcome of a formal grievance, you may appeal in writing within ten working days of receiving the decision. The appeal is heard by a manager who was not involved in the original decision, and the appeal decision is final.

## The disciplinary procedure

Disciplinary action follows an investigation by someone not involved in the matter. You will be told in writing what the concern is and given the evidence before any disciplinary meeting. The possible outcomes are no action, a first written warning, a final written warning, or dismissal. Warnings stay on your record for twelve months for a first written warning and eighteen months for a final written warning.

## Gross misconduct

Some actions are serious enough to justify dismissal for a first offence. These include theft, fraud, violence, serious harassment, deliberate falsification of calibration or test records, working under the influence of alcohol or drugs in a safety-critical role, and serious breaches of the data classification policy. During an investigation into gross misconduct you may be suspended on full pay; suspension is not a punishment and does not mean a decision has been made.

## Appeals against disciplinary decisions

You may appeal any disciplinary outcome within five working days. Appeals are heard by a more senior manager who was not involved in the original decision.

Policy owner: General Counsel.

docs.title: Environment and Sustainability
docs.text:
# Environment and Sustainability

## Our targets

Brindlewood has committed to cut the greenhouse gas emissions from its own sites by half by 2030 compared with its 2022 baseline, and to reach net zero across its operations by 2040. Progress is reported to the board every quarter and published once a year.

## Energy at our sites

The Harrowgate factory runs on a renewable electricity contract and has solar panels on the warehouse roof. Heating and air conditioning in offices are set to 19 degrees in winter and 24 degrees in summer. Please switch off test benches, soldering stations and screens at the end of the day; the night-time electricity use of idle equipment is one of our largest avoidable costs.

## Travel and the environment

Business travel is a large part of our footprint. Before booking a flight, consider whether a video call would do. Domestic flights are not allowed where the train journey takes less than five hours. Each team receives an annual travel carbon allowance, and team leads see their usage on the sustainability dashboard.

## Waste and recycling

Every site separates general waste, paper and card, plastics, food waste and electronic waste. Batteries and sensors must never go in general waste; put them in the hazardous waste bins on each line, which are collected by a licensed contractor. Customers can return end-of-life instruments to us free of charge for recycling, and we recover the metals and circuit boards.

## Product design

Design reviews for new products include an environmental checklist. New products should use replaceable sensor cartridges rather than sealed units, avoid restricted substances, and come in packaging that is at least 90 percent recyclable. The firmware team aims to support each product for at least ten years, so that customers are not pushed to replace hardware early.

## Green team

Each site has a green team of volunteers who run campaigns, suggest improvements and audit waste bins. Members may spend up to one day a month of work time on green team activity, with their manager's agreement.

## Ideas

Anyone can propose an environmental improvement through the ideas board in the portal. Ideas that save energy or materials are reviewed by the green team every month, and the best idea of each quarter receives a donation of 500 to a charity chosen by the person who suggested it.

Policy owner: Head of Health, Safety and Environment.

docs.title: Export Control and Working with Customers
docs.text:
# Export Control and Working with Customers

## Why export control matters

Some of our products and their firmware can be used in sensitive industries, and a few of our high-sensitivity sensors are controlled items under export law. Shipping a controlled item, or even sharing controlled technical data, to the wrong destination is a criminal offence for the company and for the individuals involved.

## Classifying products

Every product and firmware release has an export classification, recorded in the product database by the trade compliance team. Engineers designing a new product must request a classification before the first prototype leaves the building, including prototypes sent to customers for trials.

## Screening customers and orders

Every new customer, distributor and end user is screened against the sanctions lists before a quote is issued. Orders are screened again before they ship, because the lists change often. If the screening tool flags a match, the order is stopped automatically and may only be released by the trade compliance team. Sales staff must never advise a customer on how to avoid a screening check.

## Sharing technical data

Technical drawings, source code and test data for controlled products may only be shared with people outside the company after trade compliance has confirmed that no licence is needed or that a licence has been granted. This includes sharing on video calls and at conferences. Visitors from other countries must not be shown controlled designs during site tours.

## Travelling with company equipment

Laptops containing controlled technical data must not be taken to countries on the restricted destinations list. If you need to travel to one of those countries, IT will issue a clean loan laptop with only the data you need. Demonstration units of controlled products may only travel with a licence or a confirmed exemption.

## Talking to customers about performance

Only quote performance figures that appear in the current published datasheet. If a customer asks whether an instrument will work outside its published range, say that you will find out, and pass the question to the application engineering team, who will answer in writing. Promises made verbally by sales staff about untested performance have caused serious problems in the past.

## Customer data

Data our instruments send to the Brindlewood cloud belongs to the customer. Engineers may access a customer's device data only to fix a problem the customer has reported, or with the customer's written permission, and every access is logged. Using customer data to develop new features requires a written agreement with that customer.

## Competitor information

You may use public information about competitors, such as their published datasheets. Do not ask new employees to share confidential information from their previous employer, and do not accept competitor information that someone offers you if it looks confidential. Report any such offer to Legal.

Policy owner: Trade Compliance Manager.

docs.title: Communication and Meetings
docs.text:
# Communication and Meetings

## Choosing the right channel

Use chat for quick questions and coordination, email for decisions that people outside your team need to find later, and the documentation wiki for anything that should outlive the conversation. Decisions that change a product, a process or a customer commitment must be written down in the wiki or the ticket system, not left in chat.

## Response expectations

During core hours, aim to answer direct chat messages within half a day and email within two working days. Outside your working hours you are not expected to read or answer messages, unless you are on call. Use scheduled send when you write to colleagues late in the evening, so that you do not create pressure to reply.

## Meetings

Every meeting needs an agenda in the invitation and a named owner. Default meeting lengths are 25 or 50 minutes, so that people have time to move between rooms or take a break. If a meeting has no agenda, you may politely decline it. Friday afternoons are kept free of internal meetings wherever possible, to leave time for focused work.

## Recording meetings

Meetings may only be recorded if everyone attending is told at the start and nobody objects. Recordings and automatic transcripts are kept for 90 days and then deleted, unless the meeting owner moves them to the team folder because they are needed for longer. Meetings that discuss individual employees, such as performance or grievance meetings, are never recorded.

## Company updates

The chief executive holds an all-hands meeting on the first Tuesday of every month, broadcast to all three sites with live captions. Questions can be submitted in advance, anonymously if you prefer, and the most popular questions are answered first.

## Talking to the media

Only the communications team and people they have authorised may speak to journalists on behalf of Brindlewood. If a journalist contacts you, take their name and deadline, say that someone will get back to them, and pass the details to the communications team the same day.

## Language and tone

Write plainly. Prefer short sentences, explain abbreviations the first time you use them, and remember that many colleagues work in their second or third language. Disagree with ideas, not people.

Policy owner: Head of Communications.

docs.title: Business Continuity and Emergencies
docs.text:
# Business Continuity and Emergencies

## Purpose

Some of our customers depend on our cloud service to deliver gas and vibration alarms. This policy explains how we keep critical services running when something goes badly wrong, such as a site closure, a regional power cut, severe weather or a large cyber attack.

## Critical services

The critical services are alarm delivery from the Brindlewood cloud, the service desk for safety-related calls, and the shipment of replacement gas detectors to customers with a priority support contract. Each critical service has a written continuity plan, reviewed every six months and tested at least once a year.

## Recovery targets

Alarm delivery runs in two cloud regions at the same time. If one region fails, alarm delivery must continue from the other region with no more than five minutes of disruption, and no alarm accepted by the service may be lost. The customer portal and reporting features have a recovery time objective of four hours and a recovery point objective of one hour, which means we accept losing up to one hour of reporting data in a disaster.

## Site closure

If a site has to close, for example because of flooding or a building fault, the site lead decides whether staff should work from home, move to another site or stay at home. Staff will be told by text message and on the company noticeboard channel by 07:00 on the day where possible. Staff who cannot work because of a site closure are paid as normal.

## Severe weather

Do not take risks to get to work in severe weather. If the national weather service issues a red warning for your area, stay at home and work from home if your role allows it; if it does not, you will be paid as normal for that day.

## Emergency contacts

Keep your emergency contact details and personal mobile number up to date in the portal, because they are used to reach you in an emergency. The people listed as your emergency contacts are only ever contacted if you are hurt or cannot be reached during an emergency.

## Testing the plans

Continuity tests include switching alarm delivery between cloud regions during normal working hours, restoring the customer portal from backups, and a desk exercise for each site every year. Results and follow-up actions are reported to the executive team.

Policy owner: Chief Operating Officer.

questions.q: What happens to vacation days I haven't taken by the end of March?
gold: You may carry over up to five days of unused annual leave into the next leave year. Carried-over days must be used by 30 June of the new leave year, after which they expire without payment.
questions.answer: Up to five unused days can be carried over. They must be used by 30 June of the new leave year; after that they expire without payment [Leave and Time Off › Carrying leave over].

questions.q: I've been off ill for five weeks. Am I still on full salary?
gold: Company sick pay is full pay for the first 20 working days of sickness in any rolling twelve-month period, then half pay for the next 20 working days, after which statutory sick pay applies.
questions.answer: Full pay for the first 20 working days of sickness in any rolling twelve months, then half pay for the next 20 working days, then statutory sick pay [Leave and Time Off › Sick leave].

questions.q: What's my meal allowance for a trip to Japan if the event feeds me lunch?
gold: Zone C covers North America, Japan, Singapore and Australia and pays 80 per day. If a customer or conference provides a meal, reduce the per-diem by 15 for each meal provided.
questions.answer: Japan is Zone C, which pays 80 per day. With lunch provided, reduce it by 15, so 65 per full day (travel days get 75 percent of the per-diem) [Travel and Expenses › Daily allowance].

questions.q: If nobody answers an on-call alert, who is it escalated to?
gold: If the primary does not acknowledge within 15 minutes, the page goes to the secondary, and after a further 15 minutes it goes to the engineering manager on duty.
questions.answer: After 15 minutes without acknowledgement the page goes to the secondary engineer, and after a further 15 minutes to the engineering manager on duty [On-call and Incident Response › Response times].

questions.q: I want to spend a month working from my family's home overseas. Is that allowed?
gold: You may work from a country other than your contracted country for up to 20 working days in any rolling twelve-month period, provided the country is on the approved list in the portal. You must submit form HR-305 at least three weeks before you travel
questions.answer: Yes, for up to 20 working days in any rolling twelve months, if the country is on the approved list. Submit form HR-305 at least three weeks before you travel [Remote and Hybrid Work › Working from another country].

questions.q: I need to buy test equipment costing 30,000. Whose sign-off do I need?
gold: Purchases above 1,000 and up to 10,000 need approval from the budget holder for the department. Purchases above 10,000 and up to 50,000 need approval from the Finance Controller as well.
questions.answer: A 30,000 purchase is in the 10,000 to 50,000 band, so it needs the department budget holder and the Finance Controller [Purchasing and Suppliers › Spending limits].

questions.q: Which form is HR-114?
gold: For absences longer than seven calendar days you need a doctor's note, uploaded with form HR-114.
questions.answer: HR-114 is used to upload a doctor's note for sickness absences longer than seven calendar days [Leave and Time Off › Sick leave].

questions.q: What is QA-9?
gold: Anyone who suspects a defect in a shipped or finished product must raise a quality concern with form QA-9 on the same working day.
questions.answer: Use QA-9 to raise a quality concern, on the same working day, when you suspect a defect in a shipped or finished product [Product Quality and Customer Returns › Raising a quality concern].

questions.q: What is a SEV2 incident?
gold: SEV2 means a major feature is broken for many customers, but alarm delivery works.
questions.answer: A SEV2 is a major feature broken for many customers while alarm delivery still works [On-call and Incident Response › Severity levels].

questions.q: What goes in L3?
gold: Restricted data, level L3, would cause serious harm and is subject to legal duties; examples are personal data about employees or customers, health information, payroll records and customer calibration certificates that identify a site.
questions.answer: L3 is Restricted data: serious harm if leaked and subject to legal duties, such as personal data, health information, payroll records and site-identifying calibration certificates [Data Classification and Handling › The four levels].

questions.q: How many years of cover do Kestrel units have?
gold: Kestrel gas detectors carry a two-year warranty.
questions.answer: Kestrel gas detectors have a two-year warranty [Product Quality and Customer Returns › Warranty].

questions.q: What time is the weekly alarm test in Velmont?
gold: Fire alarms are tested every Wednesday at 11:00 at Harrowgate and every Thursday at 09:30 at Velmont; a test lasts no more than one minute.
questions.answer: Every Thursday at 09:30, for no more than one minute [Facilities and Sites › Fire safety].

questions.q: Is my dog allowed at work?
gold: The Velmont office allows well-behaved dogs on Fridays only, in the open-plan area on the second floor, provided the owner has registered the dog with reception and colleagues on that floor have not raised an allergy concern.
questions.answer: Only at Velmont, on Fridays, in the second-floor open-plan area, if the dog is registered with reception and nobody on the floor has raised an allergy concern [Facilities and Sites › Pets].

questions.q: Is there money for me to attend a conference or take a course?
gold: Each employee has an annual learning budget of 1,200 for courses, conferences, books and certifications that are relevant to their role.
questions.answer: 1,200 per year from the learning budget, for relevant courses, conferences, books and certifications [Performance and Career Development › Learning budget].

questions.q: Someone stole my laptop from my bag. Who do I tell, and how fast?
gold: If your laptop, phone or security key is lost or stolen, report it to the IT Service Desk within one hour of noticing, by phone if you cannot reach the portal.
questions.answer: Report it to the IT Service Desk within one hour of noticing, by phone if you can't reach the portal; IT will lock the device remotely [IT Equipment and Security › Lost or stolen devices].

questions.q: Do I get paid if a storm stops me getting to work?
gold: If the national weather service issues a red warning for your area, stay at home and work from home if your role allows it; if it does not, you will be paid as normal for that day.
questions.answer: Yes. If there is a red weather warning for your area, stay at home and work from home if your role allows; if it doesn't, you are paid as normal for that day [Business Continuity and Emergencies › Severe weather].

questions.q: Can I use a chatbot on payroll data?
gold: L3 data must never be pasted into any AI assistant.
questions.answer: No. Payroll records are L3 (Restricted) data, and L3 data must never be pasted into any AI assistant [Data Classification and Handling › Using AI tools with company data].

questions.q: The press called me about Brindlewood. What should I do?
gold: If a journalist contacts you, take their name and deadline, say that someone will get back to them, and pass the details to the communications team the same day.
questions.answer: Don't comment. Take the journalist's name and deadline, say someone will get back to them, and pass the details to the communications team the same day [Communication and Meetings › Talking to the media].

questions.q: How much does Brindlewood add to my retirement savings?
gold: Brindlewood matches your contribution up to 6 percent of salary, and adds a further 1 percent for employees with more than five years of service.
questions.answer: It matches your contribution up to 6 percent of salary, plus a further 1 percent after more than five years of service [Pay and Benefits › Pension].

questions.q: When is pay day?
gold: Salaries are paid monthly on the 25th of each month. If the 25th falls on a weekend or public holiday, pay arrives on the last working day before it.
questions.answer: On the 25th; if that is a weekend or public holiday, on the last working day before it [Pay and Benefits › Pay dates].

revisions.old: Carried-over days must be used by 31 May
